# CANDIDATE: NAMED_LEVEL_RSI_DIVERGENCE_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When price tests a prior‑day high and RSI shows bullish divergence (higher low in RSI while price makes equal or lower low), the level is likely to hold and bounce upward. This edge exists because RSI divergence can indicate weakening downward momentum and latent buying interest at tested support, increasing the probability of a mean‑reverting bounce.

## Mechanism

Define the prior day’s high as a named level. On any 1‑minute bar that reaches within 0.1% of that level (|close‑level|/level ≤ 0.001), compute RSI(14). If the bar’s low is less than or equal to the previous bar’s low and the current RSI(14) is greater than the RSI(14) value of the previous bar’s low (i.e., RSI makes a higher low), enter long at the close of that bar. Exit: Stop placed at the low of the entry bar (chart‑stop); target at 1× the distance to the prior day’s low, with a runner trailed by a 20‑day ATR chandelier exit after achieving 1× risk. Regime hint: Works best when VIX < 20 and after 10:30 EST, avoiding the first half‑hour where level tests are prone to false breaks.
